definitions.explanation: A case or provision that deviates from the standard rule or regulation. Often used in legal, administrative, and business contexts for exceptional treatment that is formally recognized.

examples.japanese: これは{特例|とくれい}として{認|みと}める。
examples.english: This will be allowed as a special exception.

examples.japanese: {特例|とくれい}{措置|そち}により{税金|ぜいきん}が{免除|めんじょ}された。
examples.english: Taxes were waived through a special provision.

examples.japanese: {今回|こんかい}は{特例|とくれい}だが、{次|つぎ}からは{規則|きそく}どおりに{対応|たいおう}してください。
examples.english: This time is a special exception, but from next time please follow the rules.

notes:
USAGE:
{特例|とくれい} implies a formally recognized deviation from the norm, unlike {例外|れいがい} (exception) which is more general. {特例|とくれい} is often used when authorities or organizations officially permit something that normally wouldn't be allowed.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {特例|とくれい}として{認|みと}める: to allow as a special case
- {特例|とくれい}{措置|そち}: special provision/measure
- {特例|とくれい}を{設|もう}ける: to establish a special provision
- {特例|とくれい}{法|ほう}: special measures law
- {特例|とくれい}を{適用|てきよう}する: to apply a special exception
